hyps.why: Raising an already high learning rate causes divergence.
Lowering a too-high learning rate recovers diverged training.
Low learning rates are undertrained in 243 epochs so a larger step helps.
Wider networks at high learning rates are more unstable.
Deeper networks at high learning rates diverge more.
Shallower networks are more stable at high learning rates.
Extra capacity helps when training is stable at low learning rates.
Heavy L2 underfits so reducing it helps.
More regularisation on an already heavily regularised model deepens underfitting.
Fewer updates per epoch combined with large steps hurts training.
